title: a lifted untrusted foreign Result bound to a name is charged at the binding, which is where the bound/unbound split puts it everywhere else
notes: specification/type-system.mdx:60 and :56, as for the sibling cases: the untrusted call lifts to `Result<string, Panic>` and the binding discards it. The subject of this case is WHERE. Smithers distinguishes an unbound producer (SMITHERS1301, charged at the call) from a bound Result nothing ever consumes (SMITHERS1302, charged at the binding), and 07-must-consume/result-must-be-consumed and 07-must-consume/result-parameter-must-be-consumed pin that split for authored code. A foreign call is not exempt from it. This divergence became VISIBLE only when the cascade suppression that had been hiding the whole second diagnostic was removed, which is the ordinary shape of a fix: it does not create the defect underneath, it stops concealing it. RETIRED XFAIL (go): the fork reported SMITHERS1301@4:16 — the unbound code, at the call — where the reference reports SMITHERS1302@4:9 at the binding. The cause was the one the marker named: the foreign lift was charged by `collectFacts`, the ROW-collection pass, as a bare `else` beside the row charge, so it sat outside the must-consume machinery altogether and could not apply the bound/unbound split that same analysis applies to every authored producer. The fix routes the lift through the ownership walk instead of adding a rule: `boundProducedKind` now reads the same foreign table `propagatedResultOperand` already read, so `checkBoundMustConsume` and `checkUnboundMustConsume` charge a lifted Result exactly as they charge an authored one, and `collectFacts` keeps only the row charge that is genuinely its business. A trusted call carries `kind == "never"` and is deliberately not a producer. THE CLASS WAS MEASURED against the reference across five foreign-lift shapes, and the one registered case was not its only member: `const loud = shout("hello"); return [loud]` (reference SMITHERS1302@3:9, fork SMITHERS1301@3:16) and `const make = (): string => shout("hello")` (reference silent, fork SMITHERS1301@3:30) were both divergent before this edit and both agree after it, because the ownership walk already knew a binding and a concise arrow body are not discards. The two shapes that must NOT move did not: an unbound `return [shout("hello")]` still reports SMITHERS1301 at the call in both backends, and a bare `return shout("hello")` still reports SMITHERS1101 in both.
